timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: After graduation, Madame Afterglow opened every table in Cloud Nine and announced that my first hand at each one would be played on the house. Nigga, she should have specified which house. By midnight I had won enough money for the casino's finance manager to come downstairs personally.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He stood behind the blackjack table in a beautiful gray suit, watching me turn over another winning card while Tank laughed into his drink. This nigga been counting the future, Tank said. Can't do that, I told him. Then why you keep winning? I looked at my cards. Looked at my wife standing beside me in blue silk and the ruby pendant.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Looked back at my brother. Nigga, patterns. Shawna laughed and kissed the top of my head. The finance manager looked at Afterglow. She waved him away. Let the captain play. Madame, the probability— Has met him. He withdrew with the injured dignity of a man whose entire education had failed to prepare him for the evening's central problem.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Cloud Nine had repaired its shattered windows and replaced the glass moon. The new moon was slightly larger. Afterglow said the old one had looked timid in photographs of me standing on it. I respected an owner who could learn from an event. The ballroom glittered. Music climbed through its open doors onto the roof terrace.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Adult heroes danced beside cops, singers, gamblers, mechanics, and the friends from Vegas who had arrived because Rosa told them there was a party in the sky and they refused to believe her without checking. Some wore gowns. Some wore capes. One man wore a cape over a gown and looked so pleased with himself I shook his hand on principle.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: A table near the far wall had enough champagne, pills, and white powder on it to explain why two wealthy guests believed they had personally invented dancing. Their friends moved the table farther from the orchestra before the drummer began accepting scientific suggestions. My people were beautiful in every corner. Rosa sang with Lena, then stepped offstage and let her take a song alone.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank stood beneath the lights watching both women, but his face changed whenever Rosa looked his way. The nigga's whole expression went soft and proud, and I loved seeing him unable to hide it. Mercedes danced with Petra.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Porsche danced with one Leon while another fetched drinks and the third stood near the terrace door recovering from being asked to do too much with the same legs. He's only got a minute, Mercedes warned her. Then he better use it beautifully. Petra laughed so hard the floor beneath her shoes briefly turned white with marble dust. I won another hand.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The dealer looked at me with open admiration. Sir, I have dealt cards for twenty years. You doing good. I have never seen this. Tank slapped the table. Nigga, that's what the school said! Shawna took the chips from in front of me and put them into a little velvet bag. You're finished. I looked up at her. Baby, the universe talking.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: It can call tomorrow. You're dancing with me. I stood so fast the finance manager nearly cried with relief. Excellent decision, he said. I pointed at him. Nigga, don't get comfortable. We walking past roulette. Shawna pulled me away laughing. We danced beneath the new moon with no chancellor waiting to interrupt us. Nobody asked her for a private word. Nobody threatened a locked door.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The only thing coming toward us was a waiter carrying drinks and looking mildly frightened that I might somehow win those too. She rested her cheek against mine. You like being a superhero? I like the parking. Aiden. I thought about the blue charge in my hands. The fatigue afterward. Victor sitting beside my car and telling me to listen when my body said enough.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Storm standing in the air to hold an entire school. Lena making one word travel where bullets couldn't reach. I like knowing another thing I can do, I said. Shawna nodded. That's a better answer. I had it behind the parking. She smiled against my cheek. For a while we let the song do the talking.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I could feel the room looking at us, but it stayed outside the small space between her hand and my shoulder. My fame had gotten louder in the sky. My love for her had gotten quieter in certain places, stronger where it didn't need anybody listening.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then she spun away from me, came back with both hands on my chest, and said, Show these people what all that greatness does on a dance floor. Nigga, a direct request from my wife was a sacred assignment. I did the turn I had practiced in the bathroom. Perfectly. The orchestra saw us and changed its rhythm. Rosa laughed into the microphone.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank climbed onto a chair to announce that the captain was now operating across multiple disciplines. I turned Shawna again, caught her at the waist, and dipped her low enough for the ruby at her throat to catch the moonlight. She looked up at me, smiling. The ballroom applauded. This time I didn't even pretend to dislike it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Oren Titan approached afterward with Opaline on his arm. The big man had apparently recovered from the indignity of watching me rescue his wife while keeping a drink upright. He carried a trophy he had bought himself: a small silver pedestal with two champagne glasses fixed to its top. For the man with the steadiest hands in the sky, he said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank looked at the trophy. Nigga, another building? A sculpture, Oren said. These niggas keep doing architecture to us. Opaline hugged Shawna, then thanked me again. Oren did not look smaller beside her gratitude. He looked relieved he had found a way to join it without making the whole thing about the moment he had failed to catch her. That was progress.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I shook his hand. Next time we lift the furniture together. He laughed and agreed immediately. Across the room, Claudine raised her glass toward us. The older casino guest wore enough emeralds to make Marcellus turn his head despite himself. She saw Shawna's ruby pendant and smiled with the satisfaction of a woman who had given the right thing to the right person.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna went to her. They talked for a long time. I didn't follow. Some gifts kept becoming conversations after the man who carried them had left the room. Near the terrace, Marcellus sat at a small table with Miriam and Bell. A blue cloth lay between them.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: On it rested the Blue Mercy ring, a tiny clock mechanism Miriam had brought from the depot, and one of Bell's unfamiliar engine parts. Three beautiful things. Three people who knew how much care could fit inside something a careless man might call an object. Marcellus looked up when I approached. Come admire something you aren't allowed to drive.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, that sentence leaves me very little. He showed Miriam the ring. Told her its name. Told her about Celeste, briefly, in the voice he used when the person mattered more than the story surrounding the jewel. Miriam listened without trying to make his grief resemble hers. Then she showed him the clock piece.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: It had belonged to a workshop where she worked before she was taken. She had kept it hidden because it was proof she had once fixed things for people who said thank you. Marcellus held it carefully. We could make it run again. She looked at him. I would like that. Bell quietly cleared space on the table.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The party went on around them while they bent over a small machine and gave it the possibility of another morning. I left them to it. On the terrace, Tank stood alone looking out at the clouds. He had taken off his jacket. The red ribbon remained on his wrist.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Rosa's singing drifted through the open doors behind us, warm enough to make the night feel less high. I stood beside him. You good? He nodded. Then shook his head. Then laughed at himself. Nigga, I don't know what this is. Clouds. Fuck you. I smiled. He looked toward the ballroom.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Rosa was laughing with Lena between songs, one hand at her waist, head tilted back. My brother watched her the way a man watched a door he had finally realized he was allowed to walk through. I keep thinking about houses, he said. You got a house. A different kind. I let him find the words. A place where her coat already there.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Where I don't got to ask if she staying. Where I come in and she mad I forgot some little shit, and I get to go back out and buy it because that's the problem we having that day. He looked embarrassed by how much he had said. I looked at my brother until the embarrassment had nowhere useful to stand.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, that sound like something worth buying the little shit for. He laughed quietly. You got that. I looked through the doors and saw Shawna searching the room for me. Yeah. Don't get stupid with it. Nigga, you met me. I said with it. You can keep being stupid everywhere else. We stood there another minute.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then Rosa came out and slipped her arm through his. He kissed the top of her head without checking whether anybody was watching. I went back inside to my wife. The next morning, the school attempted to hold a quiet farewell breakfast. That lasted until somebody unveiled a statue of me on the lawn. Nigga, the statue was taller than the dining hall.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: It showed me standing on the hood of a Lamborghini with lightning in one hand and a diploma in the other. The sculptor had given my chest an extra six inches of confidence. My coat blew backward in a wind that seemed to exist solely because I deserved dramatic weather. Tank walked around the base in silence. Then he looked at me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: This nigga got a permanent entrance. Shawna put both hands over her face. I stood very still. Because I respected art. Porsche took a picture from directly below its chin. Look at this nigga. Even the stone got an angle. Mercedes circled to the far side. They gave him shoulders twice. Perspective, I said. Nigga, from here he could carry the breakfast hall.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna lowered her hands, looked from me to the statue, and bent to read the little plaque at its base. They got your name right. Fundamental. Everything else appears to be a negotiation. Tank stood beside one enormous carved shoe and put his own foot against it. Nigga, you could rent this loafer. Good location. Terrible landlord. Rosa leaned against him laughing.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Behind her, two students were trying to decide whether their banner should hang across my stone knees or between the statue's feet. Tank directed them toward the knees with the authority of a man already serving on the board. Keep the entrance clear. Nigga, stop leasing me. You said good location.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The sculptor approached with pale dust still on his cuffs and a face full of nervous pride. He was an ordinary-sized man who had spent his week making an unreasonable-sized version of me. Is it satisfactory, Captain? I looked up. At the extravagant coat. At the diploma. At my car beneath the feet, every line given the kind of attention Bell would demand.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You did all that? Had help lifting. Nigga, I should hope. He laughed, relieved, and I shook his dusty hand. It's magnificent. Shawna slipped her arm through mine. It is, she said. We're still leaving it here. I looked at her. I hadn't— Nigga, your face was measuring the garden. Tank pointed at the carved shoe again.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Put that much man in your yard, the real nigga gotta knock. Storm came beside me with a smile she was not trying hard enough to hide. The students insisted. All of them? Enough of them to carry the stone. Bell cleared his throat. There was disagreement about whether the car should receive a separate statue. I looked at him.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He looked at the Lamborghini parked nearby. I remain in favor. Shawna started laughing so hard she had to hold my arm. The statue's lightning rod chose that moment to catch a harmless little spark from the passing weather. Blue light ran down the stone arm and into the carved car. The students applauded. Tank pointed at it. Nigga, even the statue got powers.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I looked up at my enormous stone face. The sculptor had gotten one thing exactly right. That nigga looked pleased to be there. Breakfast became a parade before anybody could stop it. Students lined the main drive with banners. The orchestra marched between the towers.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Faculty walked beside our cars, shaking hands through the windows, offering invitations we would never have enough ordinary days to accept. Miriam brought Bell's final inspection sheet for the Lamborghini and made me promise to listen if the engine sounded unhappy. I promised. She looked at Shawna until my wife promised too. Now I believe it, Miriam said. Jakob played his violin beside the fountain.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Not a song I knew. A song he had chosen for a morning with open air around him. Rivka sat nearby with her bag at her feet and a cup of coffee in both hands. She watched the absurd parade, then caught my eye and raised the cup. I bowed my head to her. No speech needed.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Harlan and Anne stood beneath a newly repaired arch of flowering branches. He wore the brown shoes. She had one hand tucked into his arm like she intended to keep it there for the rest of the day and perhaps several years afterward. He showed me a small flower growing out of a crack in the stone. This one wanted to be first, he said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank nodded approvingly. Nigga got good influences. We said goodbye to people whose lives would continue after our engines faded. That mattered to me more than I expected. Sky High wasn't becoming a place we had saved and could now forget. Victor would remain to train the next advanced class.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Petra had accepted a rescue-instructor post and made Mercedes promise to visit before either of them tried pretending distance was a personality trait. Mercedes kissed her and said she had never been shy about booking a flight. Porsche said goodbye to Leon three times because he insisted on making the most of his gift. Don't get arrogant, she told him after the third kiss.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You kissed all three. Nigga, I was checking consistency. Lena and Rosa promised to sing together again. Amaya had accepted a place at the academy's aquatic center, with a pool whose doors opened from the inside and a teaching schedule she had helped choose. Reiss was staying long enough to dismantle every remaining part of Voss's experiment.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: After that, he said, he wanted to see an ordinary beach with no physics involved beyond the waves. I told him that sounded excellent. Storm waited by the front staircase where I had first parked in her space. The gold sign was still there. It now read CAPTAIN AIDEN — WHENEVER HE IS HERE. I looked at it. Then at her. Dean. Captain.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: We shook hands. No accidental spark this time. I knew enough to keep the little blue current inside me quiet. Come back, she said. You sure? I made repairs expensive. You made the place worth repairing. She embraced Shawna. Then Tank. Rosa. The whole crew, one by one, without making it ceremonial enough to hide that she meant it. Victor stood beside my car.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He put a hand on the roof. One more race when you return. You sure, nigga? A fair one. No collapsing trains. No overloaded rings. No rescuing anybody halfway through. I looked at the sky. You asking a lot from the environment. He laughed. Then he hugged me, hard. Thank you, he said quietly. I held him a second longer. Stay magnificent.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He stepped back and smiled. You make it difficult to do anything else. The invitation arrived before I could get into the car. A black airship descended beyond the front gate. Its side carried a gold crown above a checkered flag. A woman in a white driving suit came down the steps holding a long envelope on a silver tray. Tank watched her approach.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, another school? I can't keep graduating. We running out of wall. She stopped before me and bowed her head. Captain Aiden. On behalf of Duke Aurelio Cruel, you are invited to the Grand Prix of Kings. The crowd around us quieted. Victor's smile faded slightly. Cruel, he said. Storm looked at the crown on the airship. An ambitious host. I opened the envelope.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Inside lay a heavy card showing a coastline, a harbor full of yachts, and a race circuit curling between pale buildings beneath a blue Mediterranean sky. The winner would receive a prize fleet and the deed to a private island called Isla Gloria. The invitation promised a month of racing, music, luxury, and competition among people who considered losing a personal insult.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, they had written me a holiday. There was a second card for Shawna. An invitation to headline one of the evening performances. And one for Rosa. She read it over Tank's shoulder and stopped breathing for half a second. Aiden. I see it. Shawna studied the picture of the ocean. Not the yachts. The water.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I watched her face change at the thought of it: sun, salt, a shore that stayed beneath your feet, a room where the loudest thing outside might be waves if I behaved for ten consecutive minutes. You want to go? I asked. She looked at me. I want the ocean. Then we getting the ocean. Tank leaned over the invitation. Nigga, it says island too.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Baby asked for water. I like to include accessories. Storm laughed despite herself. Victor shook his head with a grin that had returned in full. The messenger looked from me to the Lamborghini, to the statue behind us, to the school full of people still waiting to wave goodbye.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: For the first time, she seemed less certain about the competition she had come to invite me into. Shall I tell the duke you accept? I put the card inside my jacket, beside my badge. Tell that nigga to make room. Then I got into the Lamborghini. Shawna sat beside me. Tank and Rosa climbed into the Mercedes. Mercedes and Porsche took their red convertible.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Marcellus and Vega would travel with us as far as the city below before the whole crew arranged the next flight together. The Heart remained above us, holding Sky High where it belonged. The time door remained gone. My new power rested quietly in my hands, a little blue promise with very clear limits. The engine needed none of it to sound magnificent.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I started the car. The whole school cheered. We rolled down the open ramp this time. The proper one. The road shone beneath the tires and curved gently through the clouds. Behind us the academy rose into sunlight, scarred, repaired, loud with people who had earned the right to enjoy their own morning.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna took my hand off the gearshift and held it against her knee. You happy? she asked. I looked at my wife. At the ruby. At the watch. At the road opening beyond the windshield. Then I looked in the mirror and saw my people following. Nigga, I said, look how much world we still got. She smiled. I put my foot down.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The clouds opened, and we went toward the sea.
